author: pgaudet
body:
Benzoin (the substrate of https://www.rhea-db.org/rhea/25968) seems to be produced by plants

This is what chatGPT says about Benzoin

> Yes, benzoin is considered a natural product, but it's important to distinguish between two different substances commonly referred to as "benzoin":
1. Benzoin Resin (Natural Product) ✅
Origin: A natural resin obtained from the bark of trees in the genus Styrax, primarily Styrax benzoin and Styrax tonkinensis.
Uses: Used in incense, perfumes, and as a flavoring; it has traditional medicinal uses as well.
Composition: Contains benzoic acid, cinnamic acid, vanillin, and other aromatic compounds.
✅ This is a true natural product, directly obtained from plant sources.

> 2. Benzoin Compound (C₆H₅CH(OH)C(O)C₆H₅) 🧪
Origin: This is a synthetic organic compound, often made in the lab via the benzoin condensation of benzaldehyde using cyanide or thiamine as a catalyst.
Uses: Used as an intermediate in organic synthesis.

> ⚠️ While structurally related to aromatic natural compounds, this specific benzoin molecule is not usually found in nature, so it is not considered a natural product in the strict biochemical sense.

> Summary:
Benzoin resin → ✅ Natural product
Benzoin (chemical compound) → ❌ Not naturally occurring (synthetic)

But since Benzoin resin is a mix of compounds, I dont suppose this is what the RHEA reaction covers - right @kaxelsen ? 

This would make it out of scope for GO.

author: kaxelsen
body:
If you stopped relying on ChatGTP and read the actual articles you would see that [Wikipedia says:](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benzoin_(organic_compound))
"Benzoin is not a constituent of [benzoin resin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benzoin_resin) obtained from the [benzoin tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Styrax) (Styrax) or [tincture of benzoin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tincture_of_benzoin). The main component in these natural products is [benzoic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benzoic_acid)."

There are not many articles about benzil reductases in [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=%22benzil+reductase%22&sort=pubdate&size=50) , and none of them describe organisms that use benzil as a source of energy, only the utility of the enzymes for biotech purposes.

author: ValWood
body:
This ticket  was based on the biology in 
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11796169/
and on known yeast metabolism (benzil is not produced, and unlikely to be encountered by yeast, and therefore not an appropriate annotation).

So there was quite a bit of due diligence; CHAT GPT is only used to locate further supporting information.

I'm still confused about the action here.
Do we remove from GO, or  add a taxon restriction "never in"
Does Rhea include enzymes that are not physiologically relevant?

author: pgaudet
body: Yes, RHEA includes any reaction, but not GO. We should put the RHEA as a narrowMatch on the parent reaction (to avoid trying to create the term again).

author: kaxelsen
body:
> Does Rhea include enzymes that are not physiologically relevant?

Yes, when there is an EC number describing the reaction, we do include it in Rhea. 

Regarding ChatGPT, in this case it did not provide any useful information. On the contrary, it claimed benzoin was a natural product.
